abstract: Voting enables game-AI teams to combine recommendations from multiple engines, but their search-derived win-rate estimates may not be directly comparable. This raises a practical question: how should a team balance the highest reported score against agreement among its members? We investigate temperature-controlled hybrid voting to adjust this balance across team compositions. Low temperatures emphasize score differences, whereas high temperatures give greater weight to recommendation counts. We also examine engine-specific calibration using observed game outcomes to improve the empirical interpretation of reported scores.

Experiments in $9\times9$ Go compare four three-engine teams, from identical Pachi instances to a heterogeneous combination of Fuego, Pachi, and Ray. Among the evaluated score-based rules, teams with lower observed decision diversity achieve their highest observed raw-score win rates at lower temperatures, whereas more diverse teams favor higher temperatures. Both Logit and Beta calibration improve held-out predictive metrics for all seven engines, but these improvements do not consistently translate into stronger team play. For a team of related Pachi variants containing a substantially weaker member, Beta calibration increases the observed optimistic-voting win rate from 46.26\% to 55.84\%. The heterogeneous team achieves its best observed win rate without calibration. These results suggest that score calibration should be evaluated together with the aggregation rule and team composition, rather than judged solely by individual predictive quality.

abstract: Distributed multi-agent learning in congestion games under bandit feedback aims to reach the social optimum when each player only observes the cost of its chosen path. Existing work by Cheng et al. adapts the generalized mirror descent framework in the bandit setting of Chen and Lu from tackling Nash equilibrium to coping with social optimum. This paper investigates the framework under nonlinear congestion costs, with particular attention to quadratic cost functions of the form $c_e(\ell)=a_e\ell^2+b_e\ell+c_e$, which can model increasing marginal costs such as delays in traffic congestion.

We examine a three-point perturbation procedure based on negative, zero, and positive path-cost observations. Although this procedure provides a practical path cost reconstruction under linear edge costs, its relationship to the true social-cost gradient requires further analysis. For the marginal-cost sample-average estimator in [1, Equation (7)], we establish a high-probability error bound with bias of order $O(m/n)$ under additional smoothness assumptions. We also derive a conditional social-cost convergence result under a bounded gradient-estimation error for lin ear edge costs, showing that the social cost eventually remains within a bounded neighborhood of its minimum. However, whether the three-point reconstruction satisfies the required error bound remains an open question. Numerical experi ments with 10 players, 7 edges, and 6 paths show that the social cost decreases and subsequently stabilizes over 300 learning epochs across 10 independent runs. These results illustrate the behavior of distributed bandit learning under quadratic congestion costs while highlighting the remaining theoretical challenges.

We study the allocation of indivisible goods among agents with identical additive valuations, focusing on envy-freeness up to one good (EF1) and Nash social welfare (NSW). Since every maximum-NSW allocation is EF1 under additive valuations, the associated threshold problem inherits the known strong NP-hardness of NSW maximization under identical additive valuations and is strongly NP-complete. We therefore focus on welfare guarantees satisfied by arbitrary EF1 allocations. Although every such allocation is known to achieve an $e^{-1/e}$-approximation to the unrestricted optimal NSW, we identify conditions yielding stronger guarantees. Under uniform valuations, every EF1 allocation is NSW-optimal. Under an $\varepsilon$-small-item condition, every EF1 allocation achieves an explicit approximation ratio $\rho_n(\varepsilon)$ satisfying $\rho_n(\varepsilon) = 1-O(\varepsilon^2)$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ for fixed $n$.

We further consider the stronger sequential requirement that $\operatorname{EF1}$ be maintained after every item assignment. For this setting, we propose \emph{PriorityNet}, a deep reinforcement learning framework trained using Proximal Policy Optimization and equipped with prospective $\operatorname{EF1}$ action masking. The mask restricts every decision to assignments that preserve $\operatorname{EF1}$, thereby guaranteeing prefix-wise $\operatorname{EF1}$ by construction without post-processing repair. Across 3,000 test instances in each of the offline and random-order online regimes ($n\in[2,20]$ and $m\in[5,100]$), PriorityNet attains mean normalized $\operatorname{NSW}$ values of $0.9911$ and $0.9701$, respectively. Relative to offline Longest Processing Time (LPT) and online least-valued-bundle baselines, it achieves instance-wise win-minus-loss rates of $+27.10\%$ and $+17.87\%$, while matching the offline baseline's mean normalized welfare to four decimal places and modestly improving the online mean from $0.9694$ to $0.9701$.

abstract: Prompt optimization is essential when deploying large language models in real-world applications. Existing prompting techniques are effective in scenarios where performance can be directly evaluated using standard references. However, numerous generative tasks lack explicit evaluation metrics, presenting considerable challenges for optimizing prompts effectively. To address the issue, we propose DEPO, a novel few-shot automated prompt optimization framework. Distinct from conventional approaches, DEPO introduces an evaluator module acting as a surrogate metric, enabling reliable output quality evaluation. Notably, our framework requires only a single round of human annotation for training samples to complete the whole prompt optimization process, thereby significantly reducing the need for human effort. Comprehensive experiments conducted on multiple public datasets demonstrate that DEPO consistently outperforms existing prompt optimization and output scoring approaches.

Economic decision making plays a critical role in auto-battler games. Effective strategies must balance short-term survival and long-term growth while adapting to different game phases under multi-player competition. However, existing approaches largely rely on human-designed heuristics and lack a systematic framework for optimizing phase-dependent economic strategies. To address this gap, this study proposes a simulation-based evolutionary optimization framework for phase-wise economic policies in Teamfight Tactics (TFT), a popular auto-battler game. The economic decision process is parameterized into a compact, interpretable policy representation; furthermore, this study employs genetic algorithm (GA) and evolution strategies (ES) to optimize the policy parameters. To enable efficient policy evaluation, a simplified simulation environment is developed, in which combat outcomes are approximated using board power comparisons, and artificial opponents are generated by sampling from real match data. Simulation-based validation demonstrates that the proposed environment reproduces realistic survival dynamics observed in actual gameplay. Experimental results show that both GA and ES can effectively improve economic policies, with ES achieving superior performance. The evolved policies outperform a human-designed heuristic baseline across multiple gameplay-oriented metrics, including average rank, Top-4 rate, and win rate. Further analysis highlights the importance of phase-wise policy representation, showing that policies explicitly distinguishing between early, mid, and late game phases consistently achieve better performance. These results demonstrate that evolutionary optimization, when combined with a data-driven simulation environment, provides an effective and interpretable approach for optimizing economic strategies in complex multi-player auto-battler games.

Contextual biasing for ASR improves the recognition of rare and domain-specific terms, but most context-biasing methods involve modification of the ASR model, additional training, or changes to the beam-search decoding algorithm, complicating deployment and model reuse. CTC-based word spotting (CTC-WS) avoids these limitations by detecting target phrases from CTC log probabilities, but its offline formulation assumes complete utterances and cannot reliably handle phrases split across chunks. This paper proposes Streaming CTC-WS, which turns offline CTC word spotting into a stateful streaming context-biasing procedure. The method carries active keyword paths across chunks through token passing and applies incremental commitment to emit only stable regions while deferring unfinished keyword hypotheses. Streaming CTC-WS is compatible with hybrid CTC/RNN-T ASR models and requires neither acoustic-model modification nor additional training. Experiments on the publicly available STOP1 and STOP2 datasets show consistent improvements in WER and keyword F-score. On STOP1, Streaming CTC-WS reduces CTC WER from 18.36\% to 12.83\% and improves keyword F-score from 66.84\% to 89.61\%. These results indicate that stateful CTC word spotting is effective for streaming contextual biasing.

Real-time voice agents increasingly rely on external tools whose results may remain unavailable for several seconds. Existing evaluations, however, primarily emphasize final-answer correctness or end-to-end latency, leaving the agent’s behavior during this waiting interval largely unexamined. We introduce SpokenWait, a benchmark of 100 human-reviewed tasks across ten everyday service domains, including both one-step workflows and two-step workflows with cross-stage tool dependencies. We evaluate five real-time voice agents under controlled tool delays using stage-aware measures of speech coverage, maximum silence, response latency, and correctness. Our results reveal substantially different waiting strategies: some agents actively occupy the interval, whereas others remain almost entirely silent. Moreover, greater speech coverage does not necessarily correspond to shorter uninterrupted silences or faster incorporation of returned results, while answer accuracy alone provides limited separation among the strongest agents. A matched pending-state cue study further shows that a lightweight intervention can increase speech coverage and reduce maximum silence, but does not improve answer accuracy or result-to-answer latency. These findings establish tool-waiting behavior as a distinct and measurable dimension of real-time voice-agent evaluation.

Improving an annotation specification commonly involves revising it in response to disagreements observed during pilot annotation. Recent work has used LLM disagreement or repeated-run instability to prioritize cases for human review. We examine how repeated-run variation under a fixed LLM condition behaves as a screening signal across multiple sentence-level judgments on the same set of news articles. We use five Japanese political news articles annotated by 13 student annotators and compare their local judgments with ten repeated runs per article under each of three fixed LLM conditions: GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, and Gemini 3.8 Flash. For the indicator asking whether a sentence contains an individual's opinion (S1), the human-disagreement base rate was .44; the three conditions selected 11--17 of 68 sentences as candidates, with precision of .65--.91 and recall of .33--.43. Under the primary non-unanimity criterion, 61 of the 68 sentences were human-disagreement sentences for the indicator distinguishing episodes from themes (F2); for 20 of these same sentences, all three fixed LLM conditions were constant across all ten runs. Overall, rank correspondence between human variation and repeated-run LLM variation was indicator-dependent: pooled rank correlations over all 68 sentences were positive under all three conditions for S1, whereas F2 showed no positive rank-correlation pattern shared by all three conditions and included many human-disagreement sentences with stable repeated outputs.

abstract: Minecraft’s native keyboard-and-mouse interface simultaneously supports first-person 3D World control and 2D GUI interaction, which exhibit substantial differences in action distributions, temporal structures, and spatial requirements. In this work, we construct a lightweight behavior cloning model using a 20.25-hour subset of the OpenAI Video PreTraining (VPT) Contractor Dataset, consisting of 267 recordings and 1,405,556 frames. We propose a mode-predictor-driven Dual-Early Transformer, in which World and GUI interactions are represented by separate Transformer streams from the beginning of temporal modeling, while maintaining approximately the same total number of temporal blocks and model parameters as the single-stream baseline. Data analysis shows that the Jensen–Shannon divergence between the World and GUI keyboard distributions reaches 0.769 bits, while GUI cursor trajectories exhibit clear target convergence prior to clicking. On an independent test set with a fixed temporal window of T=32, Dual-Early improves Keyboard macro-F1 by 10.1%, Mouse macro-F1 by 41.7%, and Hotbar accuracy by 9.4%, while reducing Cursor MAE by 13.2% compared with the Single baseline. These improvements require only a 0.082% increase in model parameters and approxim-ately a 7.4% increase in pure forward-pass latency on an NVIDIA H200 GPU. Further ablation studies on the router and 2×2 temporal/head specialization indicate that the primary performance gains arise from domain-specific temporal representations. In addition, a parameter-matched multi-scale CBS(MS-CBS) module is evaluated as supplementary validation. With only a 0.149% increase in parameters, MS-CBS further improves validation Keyboard and Mouse F1 scores by 13.9% and 30.0%, respectively, supporting the complementarity between multi-scale spatial representation and temporal decoupling.

abstract: 本研究以先前台灣麻將競賽冠軍程式Rowlet為基礎，提出一個混合式丟牌處理架構，整合了原本的深度學習、蒙地卡羅模擬，以及新引進的搭配了預訓練的強化學習作法，採用循序漸進的方式來進一步提升AI 代理的表現。實驗結果顯示，我們所提出的混合式丟牌處理架構，以及相關的改進機制，在500局的對戰中，能夠擊敗原本的Rowlet版本，證實了深度強化學習於台灣麻將對局中的應用潛力。

abstract: 現階段量子影像分類受限於可用量子位元數量與電路執行成本，通常需先降低影像解析度再進行量子編碼。此處理雖可降低量子資源需求，卻使不同影像在降採樣後保留不同程度的空間結構與類別判別資訊。若量子卷積神經網路(quantum convolutional neural network, QC-CNN)對所有輸入影像共享同一組量子卷積參數，便等同以固定的特徵轉換處理具有不同資訊缺失型態的低解析度(low-resolution, LR)樣本，因此難以依個別樣本調整量子特徵擷取。 為處理上述問題，本研究提出跨解析度量子卷積神經網路(Cross-Resolution QCNN, CoRe-QCNN)。其核心不是增加量子電路規模，而是利用訓練期間可取得的高解析度(high-resolution, HR)影像，學習「樣本內容與適合量子轉換參數之間的關係」。首先，成對HR/LR影像被映射到同一個可比較且具類別判別能力的表示空間；接著，由HR表徵產生配對LR樣本所使用的量子卷積參數。因而，在固定QC-CNN電路架構下，不同LR樣本可採用不同的特徵轉換，而不需增加量子位元數。 訓練完成後，系統將HR訓練表徵與其量子參數存入離線資料庫。推論時僅輸入LR影像，先以其表徵搜尋最相近的HR訓練表徵，並使用其參數完成量子特徵擷取與分類。無須HR測試影像。 在五個地球觀測影像分類資料集上，於相同8×8量子輸入解析度與QC-CNN骨幹下，CoRe-QCNN相較於本研究重新實作的共享參數QC-CNN，分類準確率提升8.13至35.17個百分點。

abstract: 數值空氣品質預報可提供區域性細懸浮微粒（PM₂.₅）污染趨勢，但仍受排放清冊、氣象輸入與模式參數化誤差影響；既有資料驅動修正方法則多限制於固定測站或規則網格。本文將 PM₂.₅ 預報偏差修正建模為連續時空場估測問題，提出結合隱式神經表示法（Implicit Neural Representations, INRs）與氣象引導交叉注意力的架構。模型整合測站前 24 小時的 PM₂.₅ 與氣象觀測、未來 24 小時的網格化空氣品質預報（Air Quality Forecast, AQF；包含 PM₂.₅ 與氣象預報），以及查詢位置與預報時步，分別聚合測站與預報網格資訊，再以乘法調變 Gabor 網路（Multiplicative and Modulated Gabor Network, MMGN）輸出指定時空座標的校正濃度。以臺灣本島 75 個測站及 2024 年獨立測試資料評估，本文模型相較原始 AQF 的 RMSE 與 MAE 分別降低 36.6% 與 38.3%；高濃度事件的誤報率（False Alarm Ratio, FAR）由 0.774 降至 0.278，誤報次數由 23,772 降至 2,810。結果顯示，本方法在本資料與測試設定下可同時進行測站級偏差修正與連續空間查詢。

In software development, application programming interface (API) functions are crucial for program functionality. In the past, many query-based API recommendation approaches have been proposed to help software developers efficiently develop programs. However, these query-based approaches suffer from problems such as lexical gaps and semantic mismatches. For these two issues, this paper proposes an API recommendation approach, CQAAR, based on the document embeddings of community-based question-answering (CQA) information. The CQAAR approach has been applied to a query-based model BIKER model, and the experimental results show that CQAAR consistently outperforms BIKER for method-level and class-level recommendation performance in terms of the Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) index and the Mean Average Precision (MAP) index.

We audit archived neural weather forecasting experiments on 96 ERA5 single-level variables at 33×64 resolution using 27 training logs, saved configurations, and retained code. Recomputing each seed's minimum test error gives a spherical hybrid an MSE of 0.3915 versus 0.4017 for UNet++. Using the final checkpoint instead gives 0.4096 and 0.4085, reversing the mean ordering without establishing superiority. The archive supports this reporting correction, but lacks the historical boundaries needed to exclude a documented training-window overlap. Inspection also identifies unequal FFT-SHT spectral capacity and non-equivalent standalone and hybrid local networks. These comparisons are therefore retained as descriptive cases. The audit separates recoverable reporting decisions from missing evidence that prevents verified held-out performance claims; changing checkpoints cannot repair possible training-test contamination.

abstract: 大型語言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）逐漸應用於科學研究與專業知識處理，但在高風險領域中仍可能受到多輪知識探索式越獄攻擊。現有 CKA-Agent 能依據目標模型回應動態調整搜尋路徑，但候選知識主要來自模型本身，而外部知識圖譜則能提供結構化領域資訊。為探討外部領域知識對動態搜尋式安全測試的影響，本研究提出 Graph-CKA，於每一測試案例開始時由化學知識圖譜擷取固定的領域知識上下文，並結合 CKA 的目標模型回應與動態搜尋樹進行多輪測試。本研究針對 GPT-5.2、GPT-5.4 與 Claude Sonnet 4.5 進行比較。結果顯示，Graph-CKA 在 No Context 條件下對三個目標模型皆呈現較高的最終攻擊成功率，但其早期成功能力與搜尋效率未一致優於 Original CKA，顯示外部知識圖譜上下文的效益會受到目標模型與上下文設定影響。

Dynamic Economic Emission Dispatch (DEED) is a challenging constrained multiobjective optimization problem that seeks to simultaneously minimize power generation cost and pollutant emissions. In this paper, we propose EAGAMES-MOEA/D, an enhanced decomposition-based multiobjective evolutionary algorithm featuring an adaptive search framework with two complementary selection mechanisms. The proposed adaptive mating selection mechanism allocates computational resources by jointly considering convergence and diversity, while the adaptive environmental selection mechanism dynamically switches between weighted sum and Tchebycheff scalarizing functions according to the distribution of the current population. The proposed algorithm is evaluated on six representative DEED benchmark problems ranging from 5 to 40 generating units and compared with 26 existing algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate that EAGAMES-MOEA/D consistently produces well-converged and well-distributed approximation fronts under competitive computational budgets.

This paper investigates graph neural network-based reinforcement learning for deterministic job-shop scheduling (JSSP), aiming to minimize makespan. Each instance is represented as a disjunctive graph using a five-feature operation representation combining scheduling status and workload information. A two-layer graph convolutional network (GCN) with proximal policy optimization (PPO) is used to compare two policy architectures under this common representation. GCN-RL1 employs a mean-pooled graph embedding with a fixed-dimensional policy head, whereas GCN-RL2 uses candidate-wise scoring to support variable-size action sets. On 100 unseen random instances per problem size, GCN-RL1 achieves average makespans of 558.88 and 982.77 on $6\times6$ and $10\times10$ JSSPs, respectively. It also obtains the lowest aggregate relative scheduling error (RSE) of 17.5\% among the evaluated methods on selected Ft, Orb, and La benchmarks. GCN-RL2 trained on $15\times15$ instances transfers directly to Taillard instances up to $100\times20$, achieving an RSE of 13.3\% on the $100\times20$ group. These results illustrate differences in same-size scheduling performance and cross-size applicability. The implications of non-delay scheduling are also discussed.

Standard reinforcement-learning formulations generally assume that a selected action affects the environment immediately. In practical control systems, however, actions may be executed only after a fixed delay, making it difficult to associate an action with its subsequent effects. State augmentation addresses this problem by appending the pending action sequence to the physical state, while $n$-step returns incorporate multiple sampled rewards before bootstrapping from an action-value estimate. This study empirically compares backup lengths in state-augmented Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) under fixed action delays using CartPole-v1 and independent training seeds. The results show that backup length affects evaluation performance, learning speed, and consistency across training seeds. Larger tested backup lengths often achieve higher mean evaluation returns over a wider range of delays, although performance does not improve monotonically with $n$. All tested settings yield low returns under very long delays. Matching the backup length to the earliest reward that can reflect the selected action does not consistently yield the highest mean evaluation return among the tested settings. These findings suggest that backup length should be considered alongside action delay.

abstract: Our research group has been developing a Mental-Physical States Estimation System that estimates the degradation of the respective users' mental-physical states and then supports the system users' healthy daily lives continuously by promoting awareness and behavioral improvements. To achieve the above goal, this paper aims to investigate the relationships among three kinds of data regarding participants' biometric, weather, and activity log(life-log) information collected through experiments, and to clarify valuable features available for the prediction of their mental-physical states.

Experiments are conducted to evaluate relationships among participants' mental-physical states, biometric information, activity logs, and environmental information. In the experiments, participants were instructed to wear a wearable device (watch-shaped activity tracker) to record their biometric data and input their activity logs into the activity-log application we developed in this research. Experimental results showed relationships between sleep patterns and mental-physical load, between weather information and the load, and so on. However, further investigations are needed to achieve mental-physical state estimation.

In the era of information overload, recommendation systems play a critical role by efficiently guiding users toward desired information or products. Although personalized recommendations often enhance user experiences, excessive personalization can result in user discomfort and negative reactions. To address these concerns, this paper proposes a Graphically Illustrated Recommendation System that integrates AI-generated recommendations, image generation technologies, and psychological and behavioral theories. In addition, the system also employs culturally intuitive interactive elements—including selecting traditional Japanese charms (Omamori) and comic-style character illustrations—to implicitly detect user preferences and individual status in a comfortable and engaging manner. Finally, the recommendation content, which includes strategically embedded recommended items, is seamlessly integrated into visually appealing tarot-style images and positively oriented tarot-themed textual interpretations, both generated through generative AI tools including ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion. Experimental results using a virtual E-Mall with 12 participants showed that Hit Rate increased from 33.3% to 75.0% by experiencing interaction with the proposed system. In addition, their emotional responses after interacting with the system indicated that participants accepted the recommended items while showing generally positive emotional responses toward the recommendation process. By aligning with the FAD principles of Shikakeology—ensuring fairness through user-controlled interactions, enhancing attractiveness via culturally familiar and gamified elements, and embedding dual purposes of entertainment and recommendation—the proposed system offers an user-centered design that balances personalization with psychological comfort and cultural resonance.

This paper proposes a method for generating synthetic playlist dataset for context-aware session-based music recommendation. In music recommendation, users' preferences may vary depending on contexts such as activity, mood, and season, but constructing large-scale sequential dataset with contextual information is difficult. To address this problem, the proposed method extracts context-related playlists from the Spotify Playlists Dataset based on playlist names. Using the collected data as a seed, synthetic playlists dataset are generated considering context-specific track distributions. The quality of the synthetic dataset generated from Spotify playlist dataset is evaluated by training recommendation models with three conditions: training with real playlist dataset associated with target contexts (Real matched), training with context-based synthetic dataset generated by the proposed method (ContextSynth), and randomly generated dataset (Random). GRU4Rec and SASRec are trained on each condition. Recommendation performance is evaluated on test data from Spotify. Experimental results show that ContextSynth consistently outperforms Random, although it does not reach the performance of Real matched. These results suggest that incorporating contextual information into synthetic playlist dataset is effective for constructing training data for session-based music recommendation.

Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are increasingly used to derive feature-importance rankings, yet a feature that explains a trained model well is not necessarily the most useful one once the model is retrained on a reduced input set. This study evaluates XAI rankings from a performance-based feature-selection perspective. Six methods---SHAP, LIME, PDP, ALE, permutation importance (PI), and tree-based feature importance (FI)---are compared on WDBC, WPBC, and Spambase with XGBoost and LightGBM: within each cross-validation fold, rankings are generated from the training partition only, top-$k$ subsets are retrained with five seeds, and AUC is measured on the held-out fold. MIP reranking, rank aggregation, and the ANOVA and mutual information (MI) filters serve as comparisons. Across the 24 settings (three datasets, two models, and four top-$k$ values for each dataset), no XAI method is universally best: FI and PI are most often the strongest ranking, but each leads in fewer than a third of the settings. The choice of method matters mainly when very few features are kept, except on the small WPBC dataset. At larger top-$k$ the six rankings yield similar AUC and, with one exception, exceed the filter baselines; at the smallest top-$k$, ANOVA and MI are comparable to at least half of them. MIP yields no consistent gain, and simple rank aggregation is comparable to the best single ranking on two of the three datasets. These results support evaluating explanation-derived rankings through downstream retraining rather than treating explanation importance as a proxy for feature-selection quality.

Large language models (LLMs) can support spoken language practice, but it is unclear how corrections should be displayed during a conversation. We built a Japanese speaking-practice system that recognizes learner speech, checks grammar, vocabulary, and politeness, generates a corrected sentence, and replies as a conversation partner. Twelve learners used three display conditions: no text (C1), subtitles (C2), and subtitles plus panel (C3). The partner's voice is played in every condition. C2 adds text to C1: the partner's replies, and each learner turn as two lines, the kana the system heard and the corrected sentence, without marking what was changed. C3 adds to C2 a feedback panel that shows error details and repeats the corrected sentence. Each learner completed the same scenario twice under each condition. We checked whether errors flagged in the first conversation were repaired in the second. Repair rates were 74% under C1, 45% under C2, and 67% under C3. Words from the corrected sentences reappeared most often under C3, and 10 of the 12 learners ranked C3 first. Learners rated C2 positively despite its lowest repair rate. With 12 learners, most differences between conditions were not clear; the clearest was the lower repair rate under C2 than under C1. These exploratory results suggest that showing the corrected sentence without marking what was changed may not help learners use the correction.

A principal variation (PV) generated by a shogi AI can help users understand move intent, whereas a long, unbranched sequence can be difficult to interpret. We investigated features associated with points judged natural for truncation and with candidate points at which alternative moves should also be considered. Twenty-three adults evaluated two PVs for each of 12 positions. Truncation was modeled as a discrete-time survival process and branching as a binary choice, using mixed-effects logistic regression with random intercepts for participants, candidate points, and response units. The mixed-effects model suggested an association between truncation and position within the PV, whereas the corresponding GEE joint test was not significant either before or after Holm adjustment; thus, no stable position feature for truncation was identified. For branching, a tenfold decrease in policy was associated with 1.77 times the odds of selection (95% approximate credible interval: 1.69–1.86), and the Holm-adjusted GEE result remained p < .001. A 1,000-point increase in absolute evaluation-score change was associated with an odds ratio of 0.91. The association between lower policy and branching remained after excluding the first move of each PV ｗOR 1.80, 1.72–1.89; unadjusted and Holm-adjusted GEE p < .001), supporting robustness within the selected PVs rather than establishing generalizability beyond the selected positions. It also remained positive in all leave-one-question-out analyses (OR range: 1.73–1.81). Across these data, truncation and branching showed different association patterns, and lower skill-adjusted-AI policy was consistently associated with candidate branching points.

66 Shogi is a 6×6 shogi variant with a free-placement phase. We played 200 games for each of 1,440 point-symmetric initial positions using the same 100M NNUE model on both sides at 300 ms/move and analyzed the observed four-category outcome distributions and their descriptive relationships with placement features. Across 288,000 games, first-player wins, second-player wins, repetition draws (sennichite), and max_ply-unresolved games accounted for 54.60%, 33.99%, 9.70%, and 1.71%, respectively, with substantial variation among positions. We then reevaluated all 1,440 positions at 372,000 nodes/move, running two games per position with the execution labels swapped between sides. For every position, the two games produced identical move sequences, while the fixed-nodes reference outcome agreed with the modal category under the 300 ms condition in 56.3% of positions. Therefore, the proportions from the 200 repeated games per position are interpreted not as position-specific outcome probabilities, but as observed outcome distributions that may reflect variation in search volume under a fixed AI and real-time search condition. Relationships with placement features are likewise treated only as descriptive associations that include dependencies among piece placements.

Online conversations can deteriorate from civil discussion into personal attacks, motivating methods that forecast derailment before explicit breakdown occurs. However, it remains unclear whether different representations of pre-breakdown affect exhibit different forecasting behavior, particularly regarding when predictions first become correct and when they stabilize as additional turns become available. Each observed turn is represented using valence, arousal, and toxicity, with inter-turn time gaps retained as an auxiliary interaction signal. Two representations are compared: a Sequential representation that preserves turn-level affective progression and a Global Summary representation that captures accumulated affective state and trends. To examine forecasting behavior across conversation prefixes, we introduce First-Hit Horizon (FHH) and Stable Horizon (SH) to distinguish the earliest correct prediction from the earliest point at which correct predictions remain stable. On CGA-WTP, affective models outperform the controlled text baselines in F1 for the derailing class, with Global Summary exceeding the strongest controlled text baseline by 9.2 points. Across conversation prefixes, Sequential has an earlier mean FHH, whereas Global Summary has an earlier mean SH. Controlled lexical experiments further show significant gains when affective information is added to text-only classifiers, while adding lexical information to the affective predictor does not significantly improve class-1 F1. These findings suggest that different affective forecasting formulations can exhibit differences not only in final performance but also in the timing and stability of correct predictions.

abstract: Accurate multi-step traffic forecasting remains challenging because observed traffic signals contain heterogeneous temporal dynamics with different characteristics and levels of predictability. Existing approaches typically model these dynamics within a unified representation or rely on predefined decomposition rules, which may limit their ability to flexibly separate persistent patterns from rapidly varying fluctuations. To address this issue, we propose the Adaptive Decomposition Network (ADNet), a component-specific forecasting framework that adaptively disentangles traffic dynamics into dominant and residual components. ADNet introduces a learnable complementary spectral decomposition mechanism that determines the contribution of each frequency bin to the two components. Unlike hard frequency partitioning, every frequency bin can contribute to both components with different learned proportions, allowing the decomposition to be optimized jointly with the forecasting objective. The reconstructed components are then modeled by two dedicated spatiotemporal forecasting branches, and their predictions are integrated to generate the final multi-step forecast. Experiments on the Alameda and Orange regions of the TraffiDent dataset show that ADNet achieves the best performance in 20 of the 24 reported region--horizon--metric comparisons, with particularly clear gains at longer forecasting horizons. Capacity-controlled ablation experiments further show that the learnable decomposition substantially outperforms a fixed decomposition and provides additional improvements beyond the dual-branch architecture alone. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of adaptive decomposition and component-specific modeling for multi-step traffic forecasting.

Satellite foundation models provide dense representations of Earth’s surface that can be compared across time, but an open empirical question is whether the historical trajectory of such representations contains information useful for predicting the next observed embedding state. We investigate this question using 887 spatial trajectories constructed from annual 64-dimensional AlphaEarth Foundation Model embeddings across six heterogeneous territorial phenomena between 2018 and 2024. Each complete trajectory contains seven annual states, yielding a 448-dimensional representation. We evaluate a deliberately simple temporal prediction protocol in which a distance-weighted k-nearest-neighbor regressor predicts the next 64-dimensional embedding state from the available historical trajectory and is compared against a persistence baseline. Predictions are evaluated for 2022, 2023, and 2024 using trajectory-level 80/20 random splits with seed 42, as well as a leave-one-trajectory-out procedure for 2024.

Across all six ecosystems, the reproduced experiments yield positive gains over persistence at all three prediction horizons. Gains range from 14.50% to 84.20% for 2022, from 28.80% to 83.34% for 2023, and from 24.36% to 83.66% for 2024. The reproduction audit additionally resolved a historical discrepancy in the Carajás leave-one-out result: 51.60% is the correct gain against the 2023 persistence state, whereas 73.34% is generated by a historical comparative implementation whose baseline indexing selects the 2022 state. The KNN prediction error is identical in both cases.

The evidence supports a narrow empirical conclusion: under the tested protocol, historical AlphaEarth embedding trajectories contain predictive information about the next observed embedding state beyond a persistence baseline. The experiment does not establish superiority over snapshot-only predictors, memory in a cognitive or physical sense, causal territorial dynamics, universal dynamics, or direct prediction of physical territorial change.

Online news comments can affect how readers perceive public opinion. Large language models (LLMs) can generate comments that vary in stance, emotion, and tone, although readers may rely on these features when judging authorship. We examined how authorship judgments and subjective perceptions changed across an experimental sequence combining discrimination tasks with an LLM comment-generation task. Participants completed two discrimination tasks separated by a two-stage generation task. Discrimination sensitivity did not differ significantly between the tasks, whereas the response criterion shifted toward AI classifications. Confidence in distinguishing AI-generated comments decreased, while participants perceived AI-generated opinions as more prevalent after the task sequence. Their perception that comment sections reflect public opinion did not change significantly. LLM-generated comments with restrained emotion and a polite tone were more likely to be classified as AI-generated than comments with stronger emotion and a casual tone. However, this relationship did not differ significantly between the two discrimination tasks. Taken together, the results indicate a shift in response criterion rather than improved discrimination sensitivity.

abstract: We propose a novel conditional entropy function as a basis for quantifying predictive uncertainty in Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) for glaucoma detection from retinal fundus images. Using the EyePACS-AIROGS-light-V2 and RIM-ONE-DL datasets for validation, we found that our proposed EDL model regularized by conditional entropy function produced uncertainty estimates with substantially lower calibration errors than Deep Ensembles, MC Dropout, post-hoc calibration and the conventional EDL framework based on Dempster uncertainty. To further probe our models' interpretability, we analyzed Grad-CAM heatmaps using a focus index representing spatial concentration. Compared with the other uncertainty quantification methods, EDL models exhibited greater separation between the index distributions of correctly and incorrectly classified fundus images. In particular, false negatives were associated with localized Grad-CAM activations that were displaced from the optic disc, consistent with its established clinical importance in glaucoma assessment. Overall, our findings suggest that our proposed EDL framework for glaucoma detection provides not only enhanced uncertainty calibration but also admits a more physiologically consistent interpretability.

Tags that describe the visual content of anime cut scenes are a key device for retrieving a desired scene from ever-growing collections of anime videos. Existing anime taggers, however, cast tagging as multilabel classification over a predefined vocabulary, and therefore cannot express content outside that vocabulary, including object attributes and relations between objects. This paper proposes a method that automatically generates open-vocabulary descriptive tags for anime cut scenes by combining Vision–Language Models (VLMs) with syntactic parsing. The method samples the first, middle, and last frames of each cut scene, prompts a VLM to produce objective English captions, and extracts tags by matching the dependency parses of the captions against eight syntactic patterns distilled from the tag taxonomy of a fixed-vocabulary tagger. Noise tags are suppressed by stop-word rules and a manually built blocklist (87.1% noise removal on held-out scenes with no false deletions). In experiments on 1,000 cut scenes with two VLMs (InternVL3 and JoyCaption), each under deterministic and stochastic decoding, the method produced up to 28,085 unique tags—13.4 times the 2,101 tags of the fixed-vocabulary baseline DeepDanbooru, and no fewer than 7,586 (3.6 times) in any of the four configurations—with markedly higher proportions of attribute (adj+noun) and relation (noun+prep+noun) expressions. Embedding-based clustering further shows that the generated tags spread over as many as 215 semantic clusters, versus 21 for the baseline, while their principal clusters remain semantically aligned with the baseline’s core visual concepts (mean cosine similarity 0.876): the method extends both the vocabulary and the expressive forms of scene tags while preserving compatibility with existing taggers.

Inspection logs often contain only an item identifier, a measured value, a timestamp and the specification limits. When such a series shifts, engineers must decide whether to recalibrate the gauge or to adjust the process, yet from single-measurement data the two explanations are indistinguishable. When the same item is measured before and after a change point, the difference between the two readings cancels its fixed true value, and production lines naturally generate such re-inspections. Bridging-Pair Attribution (BPA) adjusts for their selection bias with a pre-change baseline, decomposes the observed shift into gauge and process contributions against an equivalence band to give a mutually exclusive four-way verdict, and requests a noise-adaptive budget of random re- measurements when evidence is insufficient. In 1,400 simulated runs no cross-attribution was observed and the inconclusive rate fell from 90% to 8–10% once the budget was met; on the real SECOM series the gauge contribution is recovered to within about 0.01h.

abstract: Accurate molecular classification of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) requires models that generalize across independent cohorts while retaining stable and biologically reproducible features. This study evaluated a transcriptomic classification framework using GSE30219 as the discovery cohort (167 tumors) and GSE50081 as the independent external cohort (171 tumors). After preprocessing, 21,752 shared genes were retained and transformed to within sample percentile ranks. Seven classifier families were evaluated using fold local ANOVA feature ranking and repeated stratified 5 fold cross validation. The selected 20 gene MLP achieved a discovery ROC AUC of 0.9983 and an external ROC AUC of 0.9010 (95% CI: 0.8322 to 0.9601), with balanced accuracy of 0.8833, F1 score of 0.7917, and MCC of 0.7191. Nineteen of the 20 genes showed consistent effect directions across cohorts, and 18 remained significant after Benjamini Hochberg correction in the external cohort. Enrichment analysis identified significant estrogen response and membrane lipid catabolic processes. These findings indicate good cross-cohort discrimination, while external LUSC precision (0.7170) and PR AUC (0.7735) highlight limitations in minority-class prediction and the importance of independent biological validation.

abstract: 針對第六代行動通訊 (6G) 環境下可重構智慧面 (Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface, RIS) 所要求之即時、動態與多規格相位生成需求，本研究提出一套基於條件式生成方法之深度學習框架，命名為條件式生成器 (Condition-Based Generator)，用以即時生成各種客製化角度規格之 1-bit 相位分布。本方法以入射角與反射角組合作為動態輸入，並於網路中導入特徵線性調變 (Feature-wise Linear Modulation, FiLM) 機制，使單一模型得以於同一組權重內承載大量角度規格之相位映射，克服既有方法須逐規格重新訓練之限制。於訓練流程中，本研究以陣列因子公式建構物理引導損失，將 Gumbel-Sigmoid 量化整合為單階段端到端流程，並參考硬體層之隨機相位預編碼概念，於量化前疊加固定隨機遮罩以抑制 1-bit 量化所致之鏡像波束；針對多波束高自由度場景，另提出啟發式神經網路混合訓練機制以突破收斂瓶頸。實驗以陣列因子公式與 Ansys HFSS 電磁模擬評估生成品質，並將模型部署至 NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 邊緣運算裝置量測即時推論能力。結果顯示，單一模型可涵蓋多種單波束與多波束規格並展現良好泛化，於邊緣裝置維持毫秒等級推論速度，且電磁模擬與公式解之主波束方向及增益一致。

穿戴式生理訊號可提供連續且客觀的壓力狀態資訊，然而腕戴式裝置受限於感測通道與訊號品質，其辨識效能通常低於具有較完整生理資訊之胸戴式裝置。本研究提出一套基於跨模態知識蒸餾之腕戴式壓力辨識方法，利用 WESAD多模態生理資料建立教師—學生架構。首先，以NeuroKit2萃取ECG、BVP與EDA等生理訊號特徵，並利用胸部與手腕多模態資訊訓練教師模型；其後，透過知識蒸餾將教師模型之機率分布資訊傳遞至僅使用手腕訊號之輕量學生模型。實驗採留一受試者交叉驗證(Leave-One-Subject-Out,LOSO)，並以Macro-F1作為主要評估指標。結果顯示，最佳教師模型 GRU之Macro-F1為0.8949；未使用知識蒸餾之腕戴式GRU學生模型為0.7175，而導入知識蒸餾後提升至0.8743，增加0.1568。結果顯示，跨模態知識蒸餾能有效縮小僅使用腕戴式訊號時所造成的辨識效能落差，並在降低感測資訊與模型複雜度的情況下維持接近多模態教師模型之壓力辨識效能。

abstract: 皮膚病灶篩檢除需辨識高風險病灶，也需將惡性病灶優先排入病人內前段候選。本研究建立以完整配置為單位的多模態風險排序選擇流程，先篩選具融合增益的模型配對，再聯合比較由預測與病人內排序、局部近鄰表徵及不同融合模型。Random Forest–DINOv2 搭配局部近鄰表徵與注意力融合取得最高 pAUC 0.170319；搭配基本排序表徵與 Gated MLP 則取得最高 Top-15 命中 294。結果顯示，聯合配置評估可辨識不同排序目標下較適合的多模態配置，且增加表徵層級並不必然帶來一致的效能提升。

abstract: 臺灣問診語句常包含口語及地區性醫療用語，使通用模型難以同時判斷回答是否切題並擷取結構化資訊。本研究針對臺灣繁體中文胃腸科問診情境，建置並評估兩個核心模組：以中文 RoBERTa 全詞遮罩模型微調的 Twclinical NER 醫療命名實體識別模型，以及以 Triplet Loss 微調的多語句子編碼器。NER 由研究者依五類實體規範完成人工標記並自行複核，資料包含 1,550 筆訓練、380 筆開發及 120 筆測試語句；依開發集選定的模型，在測試集取得 0.8526 Strict Span F1。句子編碼器使用 922 筆真實胃腸科問診回答作為正例，每筆搭配 5 個跨步驟難負例，共形成 4,610 筆 triplet；於 112 組正負回答配對取得 0.9295 ROC-AUC，並於固定門檻 0.35 下取得 0.8795 Balanced Accuracy。相較未微調基準，Balanced Accuracy 提升 16.07 個百分點，ROC-AUC 提升 15.68 個百分點。另以相同步驟分布及資料規模建立樣板合成訓練資料作為對照後，使用真實問診回答訓練的模型仍分別高出 4.46 及 4.25 個百分點。系統最後使用 Gemini 生成臨床摘要，並參考 G-Eval 以 GPT-4o-mini 進行品質評估；在 20 個問診情境中，AI 評分與護理系學生評分的 Spearman 相關係數為 0.868（p<0.0001）。結果支持真實胃腸科問診回答與跨步驟難負例有助於提升回答切題判斷能力，並完成從問診資料到臨床摘要的整合流程。

本研究提出「所見即所學」理念，開發「AI 客語隨身教」行動學習系統。學生拍照後，系統以 Gemini 為主、YOLOv11 為備援辨識物件，以 Tesseract 與 PaddleOCR 擷取文字，再經客委會四縣腔 API 取得客語詞彙、拼音與合成語音，並由大型語言模型生成中文例句後轉譯為客語。發音練習以梅爾頻率倒頻譜係數（MFCC）結合動態時間校正（DTW）計算與標準音之相似度，作為練習回饋而非精確之發音診斷。於正式環境中，三種辨識模式各 10 張測試照片均正確辨識，平均延遲 14.6 至 24.1 秒，48 個測試詞彙亦皆成功轉換為客語詞彙、拼音與語音。

abstract: We study rank-conditioned next-move prediction on the ten skill levels of the AI CUP 2026 Go training set (A–D = 1–3, 4–6, 7–9 and 10–12 kyu; 1d–6d). The nested-residual network of an open-source AICUP 2023 entry is extended from 17 to 30 input planes with ladder, 10-way rank and move-number features, initialized from its pretrained dan model in a function-preserving way, and fine-tuned on 10.6M positions. On 2.21M test positions from players unseen in training, the rank-aware model reaches 55.60% top-1 and 86.33% top-5 accuracy, 0.22 points above an otherwise identical control without rank planes (95% CI [0.19, 0.24]). No level gets worse, and the gain is concentrated at both ends of the rank axis. A counterfactual rank-swap test shows that, although one-hot labels carry no order, the model recovers the true order A > B > C > D.

abstract: 本研究探討閘控路徑規劃網路（GPPN）應用於無人機局部路徑規劃的可行性。研究使用八方向 Dijkstra 演算法產生教師價值圖，以監督式學習訓練 GPPN，並於 10 張未參與訓練的 BEV 地圖上測試 3,000 組地圖與目標組合。實驗結果顯示，預測價值圖與教師價值圖的平均皮爾森相關係數為0.9147，任務成功率與路徑合法率皆達 100%，平均路徑成本比為 1.0001。GPPN 整體規劃時間為 213.99 毫秒，Dijkstra 則為 133.08 毫秒。結果顯示，GPPN 雖未具速度優勢，仍能在未見地圖中產生接近最佳解的有效路徑。

In this paper, we have used a modular driving system in CARLA for lane selection and braking. Dueling Double DQN (D3QN) selects lanes using 13 traffic features, a deterministic executor carries out the decision, and a separate controller handles braking. Recovery can reconsider an unfinished lane change after braking. We have evaluated navigation, braking, and recovery separately. In 200 Town05 navigation cases, our system achieved 200 contact-free arrivals, compared with 13 for a Safe Navigation-based implementation. In 200 Town06 static braking cases at 20–90 km/h, the extended-speed model achieved 200 safe stops, compared with 99 for the original model. In 200 paired repetitions of one fixed blockage configuration, recovery enabled resulted in 200 arrivals, while recovery disabled resulted in none. The framework completed the tested tasks and handled the stopped-maneuver condition, although the comparisons did not isolate the route learner.

abstract: 重大建設與住宅價格之關聯可能隨空間距離及發展階段而變化。本研究以新北市住宅交易為基礎，依行政區、建物型態及坪數建立歷史價格基準，以相對溢價率為預測目標，結合捷運距離衰減、商場 Push-Pull 及建設生命週期特徵建立 CatBoost 模型。2024-2025 年共 30,007 筆時間外測試結果顯示，房價 RMSE 為 6.8989 萬元/坪、R²為 0.7857，較僅使用住宅屬性之模型降低 13.87% RMSE。SHAP 分析顯示，捷運距離貢獻呈遞減趨勢，商場則呈現非單調駝峰型態；生命週期特徵僅提供小幅預測增益。研究結果反映模型預測關聯，不代表直接因果效果。

Buddhist stories contain rich wisdom and educational value, but their abstract language can make them difficult to understand. This study uses generative AI to transform Buddhist stories into animations. ChatGPT handles text segmentation, character features, and prompt generation, while Qwen maintains character consistency and Wan 2.2 converts images into animations. The results show that generative AI can support the animation of Buddhist stories.

Enterprise AI agents require evidence that distinguishes approval from execution and observed effects. We propose a process-to-execution governance continuity model with five non-equivalent stages: Decision, Authorization, Dispatch, Runtime, and Outcome. Governance Event Core (GEC) v0.1 supplies an implementation-neutral event representation and semantic qualification contract. An OpenCode vocabulary case classifies seven claims as three PROVEN, three CONTRADICTED, and one NOT_OBSERVED. Paired isolated executions distinguish matching from mismatched request authorization. Post-submission fixtures address context drift, observation completeness, and five-stage control flow while preserving rejected mappings and post-effect failures. Seven workflow classifications replay consistently, but only five meet all original expectations. The contribution is bounded claim qualification over governance evidence, not a production authorization or enforcement system. The study does not establish cross-platform interoperability, scalability, or general agent safety.

abstract: This paper presents a fully on-device method for citrus pest and disease recognition with grounded diagnosis, combining lightweight object detection, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), a quantized small language model, and a safety guardrail. On a nine-class Ministry of Agriculture dataset (7,264/401/401 training/validation/test images), the detector achieves a test mAP50 of 0.861 and an mAP50–95 of 0.641; the eight classes unaffected by an annotation-rule change reach a pooled mean AP50 of 0.8508. With 33 atomic knowledge chunks and adaptive N-gram retrieval, a 0.5B-parameter model reaches 85.05% Faithfulness, 100.0% Context Precision, and 93.06% Context Recall on a 40-question benchmark and defends against all four boundary questions. A five-stage ablation shows that atomic chunking and the guardrail contribute most. The mean latency per question on a Samsung Galaxy A33 is 29.98 s. Reliable on-device agricultural AI depends on annotation consistency, generalization, retrieval evidence, and safety boundaries rather than a single accuracy score.

abstract: 失眠已成為現代社會普遍的健康問題，長期藥物治療伴隨依賴性與副作用等疑慮。雙耳節拍（Binaural Beats, BB）為一種非侵入性介入手段，可改善睡眠品質，然而其神經夾帶效應強弱因人而異，為既有研究尚未解決之缺口。本研究提出個人化雙耳節拍音樂誘導睡眠系統，透過分析腦電圖自動篩選對使用者有效之BB刺激組合，並結合自動睡眠分期即時判定誘導效果是否持續，若失效則自動切換下一組合，系統包含BB自動篩選、睡眠分期、入睡品質評估三部分。實驗招募3位受試者，結果顯示有效BB組合具明顯個體差異，其中兩組合對所有受試者皆有效，另五組合僅對個別受試者有效；睡眠分期模型測試準確率達0.89以上。受試者聆聽個人化BB音樂後入睡時間較雙和醫院資料集為短。本研究初步驗證個人化策略可提升睡眠誘導效果，未來將擴大樣本進一步驗證。 Insomnia has become a prevalent health issue in modern society, and long-term pharmacological treatment raises concerns such as dependency and side effects. Binaural beats (BB) represent a non-invasive intervention that can improve sleep quality; however, the strength of their neural entrainment effect varies across individuals, a gap that existing research has yet to address. This study proposes a personalized binaural-beat-induced sleep system that automatically screens BB stimulus combinations effective for each user by analyzing electroencephalography (EEG) signals, and combines this with real-time automatic sleep staging to determine whether the induction effect persists—automatically switching to the next combination if it fails. The system consists of three components: automatic BB screening, sleep staging, and sleep onset time (SOT) assessment. Three subjects were recruited for the experiment, and the results showed marked individual differences in effective BB combinations: two combinations were effective for all subjects, while five combinations were effective for only specific individuals. The sleep staging model achieved a test accuracy above 0.89. Subjects exhibited a shorter sleep onset time (SOT) after listening to personalized BB music compared to sleep onset times recorded in a dataset from Shuang Ho Hospital. This study provides preliminary validation that a personalized strategy can enhance sleep induction effectiveness; future work will expand the sample size for further validation.

abstract: Convolutional neural networks commonly reduce spatial resolution at the front end, but the effect of aggressive early downsampling on radiographic grading of mandibular third molar surgical difficulty remains unclear. We investigated this effect using 682 panoramic radiograph samples. Under the same patient-level split and training protocol, two opposite-direction front-end interventions were evaluated: the aggressive ResNet-style stem was replaced by a milder staged design in ResNet50-GN, while the same aggressive design was introduced into VGG16. Prediction concentration was quantified using the majority prediction rate (MPR), where MPR = 1.0 denotes complete single-class collapse. In the ResNet pair, milder downsampling reduced Angle MPR from 1.0000 to 0.8472 and Ramus MPR from 0.8472 to 0.7917. In the reverse VGG intervention, aggressive downsampling increased Angle MPR from 0.7222 to 1.0000 and Ramus MPR from 0.7778 to 1.0000, resulting in complete single-class predictions, whereas Depth showed a different response. These paired results indicate that aggressive early downsampling can substantially alter prediction concentration in mandibular third molar radiographic grading and that its effect is task dependent, highlighting front-end spatial compression as an important architectural consideration.

abstract: 健檢資料屬高度敏感之個人隱私，於雲端進行心臟病風險預測時，明文外洩風險極高。本系統提出一套以全同態加密（FHE）為核心之隱私保護心臟病風險預測系統，採用 TenSEAL 函式庫實作CKKS 加密方案，使伺服器於不接觸明文之情形下完成羅吉斯迴歸心臟病風險推論。本 研 究以Framingham Heart Study 資料集訓練，選用八項臨床特徵，測試集 AUC 達 0.7371，準確率 82.79%，惟因類別不平衡不宜作為主要目標。鑑於標準 FHE僅保證機密性，本研究進一步整合 HMAC-SHA256完整性驗證與密文域可逆資訊隱藏技術，使系統同時具備機密性、完整性與可追溯性，實驗證實三面向皆具可行性與有效性。

abstract: 本研究探討Wasserstein生成對抗網路（WGAN）資料增強應用於腦電圖（EEG）神經退化性疾病診斷之效果，並系統性比較常見的機器學習與深度學習模型在資料增強前後的分類效能。實驗採用公開EEG資料集（Dataset B），涵蓋阿茲海默症（AD）、輕度認知障礙（MCI）及正常認知狀態（CN）三類，原始資料存在嚴重類別不平衡問題（AD:MCI:CN≈33:4:2）。本研究以Progressive WGAN with Gradient Penalty生成合成EEG訊號，將各類別訓練資料補足至4,000筆，並評估RF、SVM、1D CNN、2D CNN及ViT五種分類模型在資料增強前後的表現。實驗結果顯示，WGAN生成資料在有效頻段內與真實EEG訊號具有高度吻合性；SVM與1D CNN改善最顯著，2D CNN與ViT則效能略有下滑或持平。整體而言，WGAN對因類別不平衡受限的模型具有顯著修復效果，但對效能已飽和的模型效益有限，MCI始終是最難辨識的類別。

abstract: 企業資源規劃系統(Enterprise Resource Planning, ERP)中之 Agent 任務多以正常流程為評估情境，對於交易遭既有後端拒絕後之恢復過程仍缺乏觀察證據證明。為探討 LLM Agent 在 ERP 既有交易約束下之失敗恢復能力，本研究將單一 Agent 接入商用 ERP 系統，並以請購單、採購單與收貨單之採購流程作為研究情境；並進一步設計輸入與參數、商業規則、狀態依賴、跨文件一致性，以及工具與系統五種受控異常情境，每種異常情境進行三次驗證，共有 15 筆觀察。當異常發生後，Agent 僅依實際系統回饋自主查詢、修正與重新提交交易，且系統同步保存公開回應、工具操作、參數與後端回傳結果，並於實驗結束後回讀交易文件及其關聯，以驗證恢復結果。本研究結果發現，於15 筆觀察中，其中有 14 筆解除原始錯誤並完成採購流程，唯一未完成者，雖辨識出過帳日期問題並提出修正方向，卻未實際執行收貨。本研究結果顯示，在保留 ERP 商業規則與交易控制之條件下，Agent 可於多類異常後完成恢復，但問題辨識、處理決策與實際交易完成並不相同。因此，於評估企業流程中之 Agent 恢復能力時，除最終結果外，亦需整合可追溯之執行軌跡與後端狀態驗證。

This paper proposes a Quantum Computational Intelligence (QCI) and Gener-ative AI (GAI) framework for human–machine co-learning in Taiwanese-English-Japanese language education with STEM applications. The proposed framework integrates multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Large Language Models (LLMs), GAI, data and knowledge modeling, fuzzy inference, and QCI with software- and hardware-based learning tools. It sup-ports multilingual interactions among Taiwanese, English, and Japanese through speech recognition, language generation, translation, and multimodal AI applications. A progressive learning workflow guides young students from multimodal AI interaction and software with hardware-based data modeling to knowledge modeling, fuzzy inference modeling, fuzzy model optimization, quantum fuzzy inference engine (QFIE), and the generation of simulated quan-tum circuits using the QFIE. The framework was deployed and evaluated in four real-world educational settings in 2026: a Software Engineering course at the National University of Tainan (NUTN), Taiwan; an IEEE CIS Outreach Workshop in Maastricht, the Netherlands; a QCI&AI Science Camp in Kaohsiung, Taiwan; and an IEEE R10 EAC Workshop at Petrosains in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. These field studies involved learners with different educa-tional backgrounds and provided hands-on experiences in multilingual AI, GAI, QCI, and software–hardware integration. Evaluation results showed in-creased self-reported understanding after the learning activities and generally high levels of task completion. Participant feedback also indicated that ad-vanced QCI concepts, hardware operation and troubleshooting, and learning pace remained major challenges. The results suggest that the proposed frame-work can support Taiwanese-English-Japanese human–machine co-learning while providing progressive and hands-on learning experiences for QCI, GAI, and STEM education applications.

Fixed test sets may miss preferences arising from an agent’s domain knowledge. We generate underspecified questions from parent and sibling concepts with source provenance, combine them with condition dimensions, and compare coded answers under a reference corpus and a corpus with an added preference statement. To search the resulting question pool under a limited budget, we study a graph-guided selector that first covers target concepts and contrasts condition values, then uses observed answer shifts to expand locally while continuing global exploration. We evaluate four adaptive selectors and no-feedback controls on fixed library, tax-filing, and dietary-guide pools of 111, 93, and 246 questions. In 30 seeded offline replays of frozen answer labels, the revised graph selector retrieved all observed shifts in every seed using 10% of the library and tax pools and 50% of the diet pool. Coverage alone matched the early result in the first two cases, whereas graph-local feedback improved diet discovery at larger budgets. These retrospective results show that structured, budgeted probing can reduce the number of questions needed to find observed changes; independent online validation remains necessary.

Reliable dental implant detection and marginal bone-loss assessment are important for interpreting panoramic radiographs. However, existing AI approaches often focus on isolated visual tasks without establishing structured evidence for subsequent vision-language reasoning. This study proposes an evidence-grounded framework for future Dental Vision-Language reasoning. It evaluates implant detection and six-point anatomical keypoint localization as the visual foundation for subsequent quantitative bone-loss assessment and structured evidence generation. Preliminary experiments using 1,792 panoramic radiographs showed that the Keypoint R-CNN model achieved 97.78% COCO detection AP50 and 98.29% F1-score, while six-point anatomical keypoint localization achieved 98.43% COCO-style keypoint AP50, 93.73% mean OKS, and 3.10% normalized mean error. Qualitative analysis further identified representative detection and localization errors. This study contributes a structured evidence framework connecting visual predictions with proposed downstream Dental VLM reasoning. The framework provides a foundation for transparent and auditable AI-assisted implant assessment, while quantitative bone-loss measurement and VLM-based clinical interpretation require further validation.

abstract: Badminton highlight generation requires precise rally boundaries, selective retrieval, and commentary grounded in visible action. We present a video-only framework combining CLTDR-GMG rally localization, I3D-based retrieval, Qwen3-VL shortlist scoring, and time-varying subtitle generation. Window-level visual observations constrain subtitle candidates, followed by deterministic text processing, visual quality assessment, and quality-eligible selection with latest-window priority. On the ShuttleSet test split, CLTDR-GMG achieves 91.55% average mAP, exceeding the evaluated baseline by 2.42 percentage points, with a 5.09-point gain at tIoU 0.7. A paired evaluation on 435 common ground-truth rallies shows lower endpoint error and higher temporal intersection-over-union under both raw and search policies. Endpoint search reduces early cuts but worsens temporal precision, distinguishing endpoint safety from localization accuracy. Separately, 68 preliminary paired comparisons from four sessions evaluate commentary-enabled reels using fixed clip selections against reference highlights. The system receives higher time-efficiency ratings and slightly more preferences, while overall-quality means are descriptively close and the reference scores higher on action completeness. These results suggest a compactness--completeness trade-off in the evaluated reels.

Monitoring social media during disasters is hampered by useful information buried in a large volume of irrelevant posts. Subtractive triage addresses this by having an operator exclude clearly irrelevant content cluster by cluster, exploiting the fact that noise has more stable features than useful information; however, the human cost of maintaining 100% recall has not been quantified. Using 33,082 annotated images from 476,827 posts collected during the Heavy Rain Event of July 2020 and embedded with a Japanese vision-language model, we examine how much the search space can be reduced without excluding a single damage image, and how many exclusion decisions this requires. Because clusters are excluded in order of their true damage proportion, the results are an upper bound for an operator who judges every cluster correctly. At the granularity of the annotation scheme, raising the target recall from 95% to 100% lowers the search-space reduction from 81% to 55%, and most of this loss arises in the last 0.5 percentage points. Finer clustering raises the reduction by a factor of 1.4(recall 100%, k=19 to k=200) but increases the exclusion decisions from about 10 to about 146. Adding post text in the same embedding space, at any of the tested text weights, yields no substantial improvement in clustering, supervised ranking, or the separation of a potentially confusable category pair. These results motivate distributing the decisions among multiple operators and replacing claims of zero loss with statistically guaranteed lower bounds on recall. This study quantifies how cluster granularity affects both search-space reduction and the number of exclusion decisions at fixed damage recall, providing a basis for designing cluster-level human review.

Multi-object image generation in text-to-image diffusion models remains challenging, as existing approaches struggle to reliably generate all objects specified in a prompt. Compositional approaches that generate objects independently often fail to capture the interactions among them, whereas joint generation methods tend to suffer from inter-object interference. In this work, we propose a training-free framework, termed conditional object composition, that relaxes joint generation methods by taking one step back toward compositional approaches. Our framework decomposes the generation of $N$ objects into two stages: it first generates a subset of $N-1$ objects and then composes the remaining object conditioned on the generated content. To enable effective composition, we adopt an inpainting-based formulation with layout guidance to preserve existing regions and encourage spatially coherent placement. To address the challenge of selecting which objects to generate separately, we introduce an attention-based scoring mechanism based on cross-attention maps and further explore the use of off-the-shelf object detectors. We evaluate our method on multi-object image generation using the widely adopted MS COCO dataset. Experimental results show that our approach achieves competitive or improved performance compared to existing methods, particularly as the number of objects increases. Further studies highlight the importance of the proposed design choices.

This paper proposes a method to refine a synthetic rating matrix for collaborative filtering (CF) to improve the recommendation accuracy for users who are receiving poor recommendations. CF is one of the major approaches in recommender systems, which predicts the ratings that a target user would give to items based on a rating matrix. The effectiveness of CF, however, is limited by the availability of rating histories. Synthetic data have been attracting considerable attention as a solution to the problem of insufficient data in CF and other machine learning tasks. Existing methods for generating synthetic data, however, do not fit a rating matrix to individuals. It is therefore necessary to introduce feedback from users into the synthetic data, so that the synthetic data are optimized to their preferences. Because it is difficult to obtain feedback from real users, this paper employs agents based on a large language model (LLM), each of which simulates the rating behavior of a user according to a given persona. To assess the reliability of ratings given by the agents, which are called feedback ratings, this paper proposes three metrics: persona sensitivity, repetitional consistency, and positional consistency. In the experiments, the MovieLens 100K dataset is used, where Llama 3.1 8B Instruct is employed as an agent. The results show that feedback ratings are sufficiently reliable and that the proposed metrics serve as valid measures for assessing the reliability of the feedback ratings.

abstract: 腦電圖（electroencephalography, EEG）具有非侵入性及臨床可近性等優勢，具潛力作為失智症篩檢與分類之輔助工具。然而，公開EEG資料集樣本規模有限，可能產生較大的抽樣變異，進而影響模型效能評估及不同訓練資料取樣策略之比較。本研究以CAUEEG資料集公開測試集之158筆記錄為研究資料，探討小規模資料情境下模型效能評估之變異性，並以EEG失智症分類作為研究案例。研究評估兩種訓練資料取樣策略，於原始單一資料切割下，所提策略之Multi-Crop正確率相較原方法最高提升7.81個百分點。然而，10折交叉驗證結果顯示，模型效能標準差達7.59%，其中超過九成的變異與測試集僅包含31名受試者所造成的抽樣不確定性相關。原始單一資料切割所估計之絕對分類效能亦約高估10.7個百分點；於相同10折資料切割下，兩種取樣策略之效能差異縮小至1.88個百分點，且未達統計顯著（p = 0.317）。結果顯示，小規模資料下單一資料切割可能造成較大的模型效能評估變異，進而影響效能估計及方法比較。採用交叉驗證可更穩健地評估模型效能之不確定性。

abstract: scRNA-seq技術能於單一細胞層級量測基因表現，有效揭露細胞間異質性，已廣泛應用於細胞類型辨識、生物醫學研究及疾病分析等領域。然而，其高維度、高稀疏性及高雜訊特性，並伴隨大量Dropout現象，使細胞表示學習與聚類分析面臨顯著挑戰。近年來，單細胞遮罩自編碼器（scMAE）利用自監督遮罩重建進行細胞表示學習，已展現良好聚類效能，然其設計主要著重整體基因表現矩陣之全域資訊擷取，對不同基因模組所蘊含之局部生物特徵關注不足。本研究提出多視角單細胞遮罩自編碼器架構（Multi-view Single-cell Masked Autoencoder, MV-scMAE），結合K-means基因分群、區域特徵學習及特徵串接融合，建立兼具全域與區域資訊之細胞表示。於十五組公開scRNA-seq資料集之實驗顯示，MV-scMAE有十二組（ARI）及十四組（NMI）優於Global-only基線，整體提升達統計顯著水準（ARI: p = 0.0013；NMI: p = 0.0001）。

Photographing people often requires subjects to adjust their poses, which can be difficult to accomplish without guidance. This study proposes Smart Photographer, a photography assistance system that integrates reference pose retrieval, body-part difference analysis, and voice guidance. The proposed PoseAlign-Match (PAM) method combines position and scale normalization, in-plane rotation alignment, common valid-joint distance, and an annotation-range mismatch penalty to reduce matching errors caused by in-plane orientation variations and missing keypoints in existing normalized keypoint-based methods. The system further employs rule-based body-part analysis to determine pose adjustment directions and provides users with text and voice guidance for pose adjustment. Experiments were conducted on the COCO 2017 dataset using 18,033 reference images and 146 query images. Compared with the normalized keypoint baseline, the proposed PAM method reduced MPJPE by approximately 16.26%, while improving PCK@0.2 by 5.11 percentage points and Precision@5 by 13.43 percentage points.

Accurate segmentation of the cardiac muscle (myocardium) is a prerequisite for assessing ventricular function, yet manual delineation is labor-intensive and operator-dependent. Using the 50 labeled cardiac CT cases of the AI CUP 2025 dataset, we benchmarked eleven 3D segmentation architectures, covering CNNs, attention-augmented CNNs, Transformer/hybrid models, and ConvNeXt-based networks, and examined their accuracy together with inference time and model size. The linear-attention variant of UNETR++ achieved the highest score (0.9037), followed by UNesT (0.9006) and 3D UX-Net (0.8946), whereas the pure ViT encoder UNETR scored only 0.8370. UNETCNX-A1 gave the best accuracy-to-size ratio (0.8886 at 36 MB), and DynUNet the best speed–accuracy balance. Per-structure results revealed a weakness that the overall score hides: only UNesT and UNETCNX-A1 reached a calcification Dice near 0.3, UNETR++ (linear) succeeded partially, and the other eight models failed almost completely. Because no labeled hold-out set was available, all scores were computed on the training cases and each model was trained once. The results therefore describe how well each architecture fits this dataset rather than how well it generalizes. We conclude with preliminary guidance for model selection.

Graph-based anti-money laundering (AML) methods increasingly exploit transaction networks, yet behavioral indicators are often introduced as isolated predictive features. We propose LIPAML, an interpretable feature-construction framework that organizes transaction behavior through a Langevin-inspired view of account state, stochastic fluctuation, interaction, impedance, and additional driving. Its core Node/Edge feature module (NE) constructs label-free node- and edge-level representations from fund-flow states, local variability, endpoint relations, route familiarity, and transaction intensity, while a lightweight propagation module adds risk-context information. On the IBM AML HI-Small dataset, LIPAML improves test F1 over Base by 2.48–5.92 percentage points across four task-adapted graph backbones. These consistent gains suggest preliminary cross-backbone potential and support LIPAML as a reusable preprocessing framework for account-level AML screening.

Automated 6-DoF robotic grasping in unstructured industrial environments requires high data efficiency, spatial generalization, and precise physical system integration. Traditional grasp detection approaches rely heavily on large-scale physics simulation data, manual annotations, and object segmentation pipelines. In this work, we present a vision-guided robotic grasping framework based on an SE(3)-equivariant diffusion model (Diffusion-EDFs) integrated with a multi-view point cloud preprocessing pipeline. By combining Eye-in-Hand (EIH) and Eye-to-Hand (ETH) RGB-D sensing with rigid-body coordinate transforms, spatial cropping, 1 cm voxel downsampling, and statistical filtering, the system constructs clean point cloud representations. Using only 12 physical demonstration trajectories without pretraining, data augmentation, or segmentation, the system generates robust 6-DoF grasp poses directly from point clouds. Real-world physical experiments on a Yaskawa MH5LF arm demonstrate an 86.7% grasp success rate.

Edge AI navigation aids for visually impaired users must continuously run object detection and spoken warnings on battery power, and adding large language model (LLM) scene descriptions can make them more informative but also costs energy and time. This paper proposes two scheduling mechanisms for the optional LLM. A power-aware mechanism invokes the LLM only when needed and restricts it further as the battery runs low, while detection and warnings always remain active. A severity-aware mechanism gives more severe hazards longer descriptions, falls back to a shorter description when time is limited, and skips the description when it cannot finish before the user reaches the hazard. We evaluate both mechanisms in a 100-seed Monte Carlo simulation built on power and latency measured on a Raspberry Pi 5 + Hailo-8 and a Jetson Orin Nano. On the Pi, average power drops by 27.2% relative to always invoking the LLM, while the share of high-severity hazards described in time rises from 13.1% to 23.9%. The results offer a reference design for future LLM-enabled edge assistive devices.

In this work, we designed a learning framework using liquid time constant neural networks (LTC-RNNs), a brain-inspired class of continuous-time neural models to perform vision-based obstacle avoidance. The learning framework is based on training data generated by the decision tree as control policy. The vision-based obstacle avoidance is achieved with monocular depth estimation using optical flow with the image streaming from the nano quadcopter, Bitcraze Crazyflie 2.1 (with a weight of 34 grams). The usage of genetic algorithm successfully identifies optimized LTC-RNN with interpretable decision making network motif. The LTC-RNN generalized well to previously unseen environments with drastic scenery changes.

As privacy regulations increasingly require the removal of specific training data from deployed models, machine unlearning has become a crucial model maintenance mechanism for privacy-aware intelligent systems. This challenge is particularly significant for Vision Transformers (ViTs), whose non-local self-attention and distributed representations make selective forgetting difficult without full retraining. This work studies machine unlearning in ViTs through a weight-resetting unlearning framework. Specifically, we compare three resetting strategies: magnitude-based reset (as an unstructured pruning baseline), gradient-based reset, and attention head reset. We formally decouple the conceptual multi-objective unlearning goal from the practical two-stage resetting-and-recovery pipeline, and formulate parameter importance at an element-wise scalar resolution. Experiments are conducted on CIFAR-100 under the forget-10 setting alongside benchmark baselines and efficiency profiling. The results demonstrate that while all three resetting methods achieve near-complete forgetting after post-fine-tuning, gradient-based reset achieves the most favorable balance between forgetting effectiveness, retain accuracy recovery, and reference model alignment, yielding an ≈ 8.3× speedup over full retraining. Furthermore, intervention scope analysis indicates that targeted parameter resetting in late-stage transformer blocks is sufficient to induce zero-retrain forgetting, offering practical insights for sustainable and privacy-compliant vision deployments.

This paper proposes a learning model for classifying the presence or absence of fouls during basketball layup shots using multi-view still images. In the proposed method, still images obtained at the same time from six cameras positioned at different viewpoints are treated as a single input set, and the presence or absence of fouls is classified by fusing the features extracted from each image. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, its performance was compared with that of a conventional method using single-view images. The results showed that the proposed method outperformed the conventional method on all evaluation metrics: Accuracy, Recall, Precision, Specificity, and F1 Score. These results demonstrate that fusing and utilizing multi-view information is effective for improving foul classification performance during layup shots.

While most video-camera-based gaze estimation methods target a single user, few multi-user studies have investigated per-user per-sonalized facial-landmark models or quantified how anatomical feature partitioning and screen-region granularity affect estimation performance. This study proposes a video-camera-based system that simultaneously estimates the gaze points of two users sharing a screen. The proposed system applies principal component analysis (PCA) to 3D facial landmarks extracted from video images to construct compact facial features. A non-person-specific model (base model) is built before applying each user’s 9-point personal calibration, and the gaze estimation results of multiple users are output simultaneously. We evaluated the proposed system with 18 participants across evaluation screens divided into 9 regions (evaluating accuracy at calibrated positions) and 16 and 25 regions (evaluating spatial generalization to unseen positions). The method separating the eye region yielded the highest sample mean gaze-region accuracies of 95.06%, 88.12%, and 78.44% under the single-user condition and 91.98%, 77.71%, and 64.00% under the two-user condition, respectively.
